en.title: Minimum Total Cost of Merging Any Two Numbers
en.description:
Each time, choose elements at two different positions, remove them, and insert their sum; the cost of this step is that sum. Find the minimum total cost to merge everything into a single element.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n positive integers; full original bounds 2≤n≤100000, 1≤a[i]≤100.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 85; 2; 28. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Repeatedly pop the two smallest items from a min-heap, add their sum to the total, and push the sum back.
